newsitem.title: JORDAN: British jet car prepares for desert debut.
newsitem.headline: British jet car prepares for desert debut.

text.p: Britain's world land speed record challenger, the jet-powered Thrust SSC, could make its debut test run in the deserts of southern Jordan on Tuesday, organisers said on Monday.
They hoped the 9.5-tonne "car", powered by twin jets from a Phantom warplane, would make two or three runs on the mudflats of al-Jafr, nearly 200 km (125 miles) south of Amman.
But their plans could still be frustrated by the weather.

"It's been very windy. We had a sandstorm today and we're just praying it will be calm," said Andrew Noble, whose brother Richard is leading the Thrust team challenge to break his own world record of 633.47 mph (1,019.44 kph), set in 1983.
"The car is ready...and everything is tested," he added.
Tuesday's trials are not expected to take the car much above a sedate 200 mph (320 kph).
Noble said driver Andy Green, a British Royal Air Force pilot, would build up speed over subsequent outings in his bid to become the fastest man on four wheels.

The Thrust team, who say the car is designed ultimately to reach speeds as high as 850 mph (1,360 kph) hope their runs in Jordan will set the stage for an attempt next year on the sound barrier -- about 750 mph (1200 kph).

Apart from fine tuning the car's 110,000 horsepower jet engines, team members have spent the last two weeks trudging the 16 kilometre (10 mile) tracks on the desert floor, picking out small stones that could damage the car's solid aluminium wheels.

Organisers have painted 17 of the tracks, about 15 metres (50 ft) apart, on the desert floor. The car will follow each track just once because its metal wheels will dig into the desert floor as it speeds by.
To reach the speed of sound and still have time for its parachute brakes to slow it, the car would need a track of over 15 miles (22.5 km).
